GATCHALIAN City of Valenzuela The City Hail, MacArthur Highway Karuhatall, Vaienzuela City 1440 Dear Mayo€ f ;uchalian: This has reference to your letter dated 10 October 2013 seeking this Department's opinion on "whether or not the necessity of upgrading/raising of roads and drainage system by a local government unit falls within the purview of 5.0, 5.1.7 or 5.1.8 of the Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2013-1 (JMC No. 2013-1) issued on 25 March 2013 by the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC), Department of Budget and Management (DBM) and this Department." At - outset, may we invite your attention to the definition of disaster prevention and mitigaae•y under RA 10121 or the Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010: Mitigation" is the lessening or limitation of the adverse impacts of hazards a •red disasters. Mitigation measures encompass engineering techniques and hazard-resn:ant construction as well as improved environmental policies and public awareness. "Mitigation" refers to the structural and non-structural measures undertaken to limit the adverse impact of natural hazards, environmental degradation, and technological hazards and to ensure the ability of at-risk communities to address vulnerabilities aimed at minimizing the impact of disasters. Such measures include, but are not limited to, hazard-resistant construction and engineering works, the formulation and implement-: ion of plans, programs, projects and activities, awareness raising, knowledge managemer•• . policies on land-use and resource management, as well as the enforcement of compreh live land-use planning, building and safety standards, and legislation.2 Section 3(i!

"Disaster Prevention" , on the other hand, is the outright avoidance of adverse impacts of hazards and related disasters. It expresses the concept and intention to completely potential adverse impacts through action taken in advance such as constructic:j ei dams or embankments that eliminate flood risks, land-use regulations that do not permit any settlement in high-risk zones, and seismic engineering designs that ensure the survival and function of a critical building in any likely earthquake.3 We can see that the essence of disaster prevention and mitigation are merely reiterated in JMC No. 2013-1 and the enumerated activities appears to be not exclusive as the guidelines permit the conduct of projects and activities that are of similar nature and considered necessary in disaster prevention and mitigation. Not being exclusive, the project activities to be performed other than those enumerated must satisfy the conditions that they must be "of similar nature and considered necessary". Referring to JMC No. 2013-1, is the intended upgrading/raising of roads and drainage system an activity that is of similar nature to and necessary, taking into account the following enumerated project activities from JMC No. 2013-1): "Projects and Activities: 51.1 Conduct of risk assessment, vulnerability analysis, and other science-based technology and methodologies to enhance LGU ecological profile, sectoral studies and Inainstream disaster risk reduction and management activities / Climate Change Adaptation(CCA) in Comprehensive Land Use Program (CL UP) and Comprehensive Development PrograM(CDP); 5.1.2 Implement Community-Based Monitoring System (CBMS) with disaster risk reduction and management ,/CCA indicators; 5.1.3 C,åpability building (train, equip, organize, provide funding, sustain) on mainstreaming disaster risk reduction and management/CCA in development planning, investment programming/financing, and project •aluation and development; 5. Cbnduct of activities to review and integrate disaster risk reduction and management /CCA into various environmental policies, plans, programs, and projects; 5.1.5 Conduct vulnerability analysis and risk assessment for critical facilities and infrastructure; 5.1.6 Development oftools on risk assessment; Section 3(k), KA

51.7 Construction of dams or embankments that will reduce/mitigate flood risks; and 5. I. g Other programs or projects of similar nature and considered necessary. " The föregoing project activities essentially target measures for disaster prevention and mitigation. To determine further what may appropriately be covered as permissible project where the LDRRMF may be allocated and utilized, references to other authoritative materials on the subject were made. For developing nations, such as ours, prevention is perhaps the most critical components in managing disasters, however, it is clearly one of the most difficult to promote. What is clear is that disaster prevention refers to measures taken to eliminate the rootcauses that make people vulnerable to disaster. 4 Mitigation reduces and limits the destructive and disruptive effects of hazards on the elements at risk. Measures range from the physical such as engineering works like bridges, protective dikes, embankments, and safe building design to the non-structural interventions such as community risk assessment, community risk reduction planning, public awareness, food security programs, group savings, cooperatives, crop insurance, strengthening community disaster management organizations and advocacy on disasters and development issues, legislation and land use zoning. Mitigation and prevention interventior:s are directly linked to development planning. "Disaster mitigation is intrinsic to sustainable development" (Twigg et al, Given the foregoing premises, we are of the view that the activity, "upgrading/raising of roads and drainage system" falls within the permissible projects under the disaster prevention and mitigation measures where LDRRMF may be allocated and utilized, provided that these activities must be directly linked to development planning aimed to eliminate and/or limit the rootcauses that expose and make the community vulnerable to disasters. To borrow the quotation from the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNISDR)6 . "Invest in and maintain critical infrastructure that reduces risk, such as flood drainage, adjusced where needed to cope with climate change" Community Based Approaches to Disaster Mitigation by Lorna Victoria (2007).
